pass_a_gloss: CYR.: (or how would) this be understood of newness? And how would some still also be called new dough, if a remnant of leaven remains in them, and they would be not wholly without share of the unholy and loathsome baseness? One must conceive then, according to the reasoning befitting the contemplations, a form of another leaven, not having in itself the need to be blamed, but rather even marveled at by the God-inspired Scripture. To leaven then the Savior compares the renowned and profit-bearing power of the divine and evangelical training, saying: 'The kingdom of the heavens is like leaven, which a woman having taken hid in three measures of flour, until the whole was leavened.' For entering into mind and heart, the life-making energy of the evangelical training changes over soul and body and spirit as it were toward its own quality. Therefore with such leaven it would be fitting to suspect the peoples to have been leavened, as brought in the form of the loaves, and each from two tenths; the type writing down for us in riddle the as-it-were double of the training. PALL.: Such as what do you say? CYR.: For would you not say, O Palladius, that through double training, legal and evangelical, we will be holy and well-acceptable to God, and we may go thus into new and choice life? PALL.: I say. CYR.: This indeed also the Savior himself made clear to us, saying: 'On account of this I said to you that every scribe discipled in the kingdom of the heavens is like a rich man, who casts out from his treasure new things and old.' For those having the mind knowing the things decreed through Moses, and filled with that ancient and as in types commandment, then besides that having become rich in the new and evangelical knowledge, boast for the rest, I think, of a double training too. PALL.: You said rightly. CYR.: But not in loaves alone was the multitude of those prepared for newness of life drawn for us, but the law commands in addition that seven lambs must be brought with the one calf, and two rams; a libation plainly following the victims, that is wine poured down, and as in a fourth of the hin, which is six xestai, pronounced in the tongue among us. Therefore the seven lambs again would be a type of the flock of the believers, being infant in Christ; for symbol of infancy the lamb; except as in strength and spiritual manliness advancing into perfection and into measure of stature of the fullness of Christ. PALL.: How did you say? CYR.: Having named the lambs, then putting in the calf through the middle, he adds the rams. And the lambs would be a type of the flock; and of strength and manliness the calf, for the animal is strong; and of complete age for the rest the rams. Therefore the believers, through being wont to master manfully the earth(lier things) (continues)
pass_b_english: Cyril: …this be understood as newness? And how could some still be called a new dough, if a remnant of leaven stays in them and they have not wholly parted from unholy and loathsome wickedness? We must therefore conceive, by the reasoning that fits such contemplations, of another kind of leaven, one that has nothing in itself to be blamed, but is rather even admired in the inspired Scripture. So the Savior likens the renowned and beneficial power of the divine and gospel training to leaven, saying: ‘The kingdom of heaven is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until the whole was leavened’ (Matthew 13:33). For the life-giving working of the gospel training, sinking into mind and heart, changes soul and body and spirit, as it were, into its own quality. So it would be fitting to suppose that the peoples are leavened with such leaven, brought as they are in the form of the loaves, each of two tenths; the type depicting for us in a riddle the twofold, as it were, character of the training.
Palladius: What exactly do you mean?
Cyril: Would you not say, Palladius, that through a twofold training, of the law and of the gospel, we shall be holy and acceptable to God, and so go forward into a new and choice life?

Cyril: The Savior himself made this clear to us, saying: ‘Therefore I said to you that every scribe who has been made a disciple in the kingdom of heaven is like a rich man who brings out of his treasure things new and old’ (Matthew 13:52). For those whose mind knows what was decreed through Moses and has been filled with that ancient commandment given in types, and who on top of it have grown rich in the new knowledge of the gospel, can boast from then on, I think, of a twofold training.

Cyril: But the multitude of those prepared for newness of life was not depicted for us in the loaves alone. The law further commands that seven lambs be brought, with the one calf and two rams; and plainly a drink offering follows the victims, that is, wine poured out, a fourth part of a hin, which is six xestai, as it is called in our language. So the seven lambs in turn would be a type of the flock of believers, a flock still in infancy in Christ, for the lamb is a symbol of infancy, yet advancing, as in spiritual strength and manliness, to perfection and to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ (Ephesians 4:13).

choices.why: Cyril's text of Matthew 13:52 reads 'rich man' where the Gospel has 'householder'; kept as he gives it.
Cyril's own conversion of the quarter hin; the unit name kept.
